questions.stem: A scatter graph shows a strong correlation between ice cream sales and drowning incidents. Does this mean ice cream causes drowning?

options.text: No, correlation does not imply causation — a third variable (e.g. hot weather) likely causes both
Yes, because the correlation is strong
No, because the correlation must be negative

questions.explanation: Correlation does not imply causation. Both ice cream sales and drowning incidents increase in hot weather, which is the lurking variable. Ice cream does not cause drowning.

questions.stem: On a scatter graph, a point that does not fit the general pattern is called:
questions.explanation: A data point that does not follow the general trend is called an outlier (or anomaly). It may be due to an error in data collection or an unusual circumstance.
